Sreedhara Murthy.P vs Rupeesh Kumar on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33230375/
1

The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 15.02.2023.
2.

The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 15.02.2023 at about 11.00 a.m., the petitioner was proceeding in his motorcycle bearing No.KA-50-EE- 3920 from Bettahalasur to Yelahanka side slowly and cautiously, when he proceeding on Bettahalasur service road, near Bank of India, at that time the rider of Splendor Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50-EF-3725 came from opposite side in a rash and negligent manner without following traffic rules and regulations
all of a sudden came from right side turn and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Prolife Multi-speciality Hospital,
wherein he was admitted as inpatient and he has spent more than Rs.3,00,000/-
towards hospitalization charges, treatment medicines, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges etc.,

Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy and he was working as Security Guard at Cytecare Hospital, Venkatala,
Bagalur, Yelahanka and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue his work and is under complete bed rest and he is suffering from permanent disability.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
prays to award compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notices, respondents appeared before the tribunal through their counsels and filed separate written statement.
The respondent No.1- owner appeared through his counsel and filed written statement by stating that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further he has admitted that the he is the RC owner of the alleged offending motorcycle bearing No.KA-50-EF- 3725 and the 2nd respondent is the insurer and also the policy was in force as on the date of the accident.

Hence,
claim if any has to be contested against the insurance company i.e., Respondent No.2.

Respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by admitting the issuance of policy to the motorcycle bearing No.KA-50-EF-3725 and the liability of this respondent,
if any, is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further contended that, the accident was caused due to negligence on the part of the petitioner.
Also contended that the rider of the offending motorcycle was not having valid and effective driving licence and insured vehicle had no FC as on the date of alleged accident.
Further contended non -compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Further denied the age, avocation, alleged disability and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.

Hence, the respondent No.2 prays to Sreedhara Murthy.P vs Rupeesh Kumar on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33230375/
2 dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievious in- juries due to the actionable negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50-EF-3725 by its rider, in RTA took place on 15.12.2023 at about 11.00 a.m near Bank of India, Betta- halasuru to Yalahanka service road, Bettahalasuru, Bengaluru?

2. 
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
3 . What order or award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 15 & 23.
Also examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P16 to 20.
Dr.S.A. Somashekara examined as PW.3 and got marked Ex.P21 & 22.
The respondent No.1 got himself examined as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.5 documents.
In spite of sufficient opportunity the respondent No.2-insurance company has not lead any evidence in support of their defence.

6. Heard the arguments and perused evidence that are available on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final orders

for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:

ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar along with sketch, IMV report, wound certificate,
charge sheet and IMV notice and reply which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 9.
9.
On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR is registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information given by the petitioner himself.

The said Ex.P.2 statement of the petitioner was recorded on the same day of Sreedhara Murthy.P vs Rupeesh Kumar on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33230375/
3 accident by police in the presence of the doctor.
In the Ex.P2 the informant alleged the rash and negligent driving by the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No. KA-50-EF-3725.
After the registration of FIR as per Ex.P1, the Ex.P3 spot mahazar and Ex.P.4 rough sketch was conducted.

On perusal of the contents of Ex.P3 spot mahazar and Ex.P.4 rough sketch the petitioner was proceeding in the left portion of the road and the rider motorcycle bearing No.KA-50-F- 3725 came from opposite side and by changing his line dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
10. The rider of the motorcycle is the respondent No.1 and the respondent No.1 has also examined himself as RW.1 by denying his negligence.
Except his oral evidence the RW.1 has not produced any other evidence to disbelieve the contents of mahazar and rough sketch marked at Ex.P.3 and 4.
In his evidence the RW.1 has not denied the spot of the accident and the manner in which the accident was caused as mentioned in Ex.P.3 and P4.
As per the rough sketch and the mahazar the respondent No.1 was proceeding in the left side road changed his lane and entered into the extreme right side of service road and caused the accident.
The said fact is not denied by the respondent No.1, as such no evidence is available to hold the contributory negligence by the petitioner.
The main cause for the accident is the rider of the offending motorcycle has came to his extreme right side and caused the accident.
The Ex.P.5 is IMV report wherein the motorcycle of the petitioner has got damaged in front and right side and the same way the the offending motorcycle also got damaged in the front right side.

Thereby, the IMV report also supported the contents of mahazar where it shows that the respondent No.1 went to his extreme right side and dashed against the right side portion of the motorcycle of the petitioner.

The contents of Ex.P.3 to P5 mahazar, rough sketch and IMV report helped the petitioner to prove his case and alleged negligence of the respondent No.1.
11.
The petitioner examined himself as PW.1 by deposing the negligence of respondent No.1 and produced Ex.P.1 to P9 documents in support of his case.
The PW.1 was cross-examined at length and respondent No.1 examined himself by denying his negligence.
The respondent No.1 failed to rebut the case of the petitioner which is supported by Ex.P.1 to P9.
Thereby the contention of the respondent No.1 and 2 cannot be accepted in respect of contributory negligence by the petitioner.
Thus, it can be concluded that, the main negligence is on the part of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50-EF-3725 as he came to his extreme right side and caused the accident.

Thus, the petitioner established the negligence on the part of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50-EF-3725.
12.
There is no delay in registering the FIR.
The Ex.P.17 and P18 MLC and police intimation establishes the fact of accident.
Ex.P7 charge sheet is also came to be filed on the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 50-EF-3725.
The IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50- EF-3725.
No grounds are made out by the respondents to show that contributory negligence from the petitioner and also to disbelieve the contents of charge sheet.
13. The respondent No.2 has filed written statement by denying the negligence and their liability but not lead any evidence.
As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA- 50-EF-3725.
Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident is caused by the rash and negligent riding by Sreedhara Murthy.

4 the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-50-EF-3725.
14.
The respondent no.1 and 2 even though filed written statement, has failed to establish the negligence on the part of petitioner for the occurrence of the accident.
The charge sheet is came to be filed on the rider of the motorcycle bearing No KA-50-EF-3725 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 337 & 338 of IPC & Sec.134 (a) & (b) r/w 187 of IMV Act.

sentences.text: Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

15. By relying on the said precedent and in the absence of rebuttal evidence and denial in respect of police documents marked at Ex.P1 to 9, this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50-EF-3725.
16.

In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

sentences.text: The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

18. In support of these documentary evidence, if we perused the oral evidence of the petitioner on this point, even though the respondent no.2 made a suggestions to the petitioner by stating that the accident was occurred by his negligence, nothing being elicited or produced to probabalise the said defence.
19. The contents of Ex.P3 spot mahazar falsifies the contention of respondent no.2 about the contributory negligence of petitioner for the occurrence of accident.

In this context by considering the contents of Ex.P1 to 9 this court tilts in favour of the petitioner as the petitioner has to prove the alleged negligence on the basis of the evidence and proof of the same on preponderance of probabilities.

Sreedhara Murthy.P vs Rupeesh Kumar on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33230375/
5 20.
As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 15.02.2023 which is caused by the rider of the motorcycle bearing No. No.KA-50-EF- 3725 which belonging to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
21.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:-
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 47 years.
The petitioner produced the copy of Aadhaar card.

As per the discharge summary marked marked at Ex.P10 the petitioner sustained right patella fracture,
right proximal tibia fracture (Intra articular).
By considering the nature of injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.60,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
b) Medical expenses: The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P12 amounting to Rs.2,42,334/-.
These bills are also supported with the case records produced by the PW.2 & 3 and no grounds are made out to disbelieving these bills.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitle for the reimbursement of the same by rounding of the same i.e., Rs.2,42,500/-.
c) Loss of income during laid up period and Loss of Future income:
The petitioner has stated that he was working as Security Guard and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has produced any pay slips or documents pertaining to his avocation.
It is alleged by the petitioner that after the accident due to the disability he is removed from the service and he can produce the documents to show his removal from service.

The petitioner produced Ex.P.23 bank statement wherein as admitted in his cross- examination that on 21.06.2023 he has received Rs.95,362/-
under the head of salary and on 21.11.2023 he has received Rs.48,151/-.
Even though he has admitted the receipt of said amount, he has stated that the said amount is PF and gratuity.
The answers given by the PW.1 regarding his employment and his termination and also the payment received by him is hereby quoted for better appreciation of this point:
"  Cyte care cancer     .

,   apply .
As answered by the PW.1 he has the documents to show that he is removed from the service and also he was having PF and ESI facility.

The PW.1 also admitted in his cross-examination that he has no problem to produce the said document to show that he is removed from the service and has not availed the benefit of ESI for the period for which he was absent to his job.
It is further very important to note that the petitioner has not produced any documents to show that he has not got any salary fro the period he was under the treatment.
As admitted by the PW.1 he has the documents to show that he removed from the service, but no such documents are produced before this tribunal.
To over come the said allegation, the petitioner has not produced any evidence.

The petitioner has not produced any documents to show that,
he is removed from service.
The up to date account statement or salary slips or the relieving letter is not produced by the petitioner.

The petitioner has not examined his employer to prove that during the recovery period he was not getting salary or the benefits from the ESI and later he is removed from the service due to disability caused by the injuries of the accident.
No such efforts or evidence is placed by the petitioner to show that he is not continued with earlier job/avocation.
Even in the petitioner has not produced documents to show that he has obtained leave for which he has not got salary.

In spite of sufficient opportunity the petitioner neither examined his employer nor produced any documents to show that, he has left the Sreedhara Murthy.P vs Rupeesh Kumar on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33230375/
7 said job due to the permanent disability caused to him by the accident.

sentences.text: The further account statement is also not produced.
The relieving letter or the copy of resignation letter is also not produced.

In this regard if he rely on Section 114 of Evidence Act which states as follows;
Section 114. Court may presume existence of certain facts.

The Court may presume the existence of any fact which it thinks likely to have happened, regard being had to the common course of natural events, human conduct and public and private business, in their relation to the facts of the particular case.
Illustrations

The Court may presume - (g) that evidence which could be and is not produced would, if produced, be unfavourable to the person who withholds it;
When a party has evidence with him to prove the existence of few facts and if such party has not produced those documents and offers no explanation of non production of such evidence the adverse inference has to be drawn.

By applying the said principle of law in this case the petitioner has not produced any documents to show that, he is not continued in service, the adverse inference has to drawn by holding that, the petitioner continued in service.
The salary slips also not produced to substantiate the entries in Ex.P.23 account statement.
The petitioner has not produced any documents to show that, he has availed the leave due to which he has got loss of pay.
By considering the same this tribunal is holding that, the petitioner has not sustained any future loss.

Accordingly,
the question of awarding compensation towards loss of future income does not arise.'

That is to say as the actual financial loss arising out of physical disability is not made out by the claimant, he is not entitled for compensation towards 'loss of future income' and loss of income during laid up period.
d) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;
As per Ex.P10 discharge summary, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 8 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P6 the injuries sustained by the petitioner is grievous in nature.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
e) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 8 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

By considering the nature of the fracture as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e.,
Rs.8,000/- in total as the petitioner has spent 8 days in the hospital.

f) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
Sreedhara Murthy.P vs Rupeesh Kumar on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33230375/
8
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.

As per the evidence of PW.3 doctor the fracture to patella is united and another proximal tibia is partially united and the said partially united fracture may take another one or two months to get united.

Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.60,000/-
under this head.
g)Towards future medical expenses: PW.3 stated that the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants, which may costs Rs.50,000/-.
By looking to the nature of injuries sustained the treatment taken, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.40,000/- under this head.

a) Towards pain and agony Rs. 60,000/-
b) Towards Medical expenses Rs. 2,42,500/-
c) Towards loss of income and loss -NIL- of disability d) Towards food nourishment and Rs. 50,000/-
conveyance e) Towards attendant charges Rs. 8,000/-

f) Towards loss of amenities Rs. 60,000/-
g) Towards future medical Rs. 40,000/-
expenses
Total Rs
22 . Liability:-
According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 & 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.2 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the motorcycle bearing No.KA-50-EF-3725 and the policy was in force at the time of accident.
The charge sheet is also silent and no other offences are invoked against the respondent No.1 by alleging the driving of the said motorcycle without valid licence.
No other grounds are made out by showing the violation of policy condition by the respondent No.1.
The respondent No.1 produced his driving licence as Ex.R2.

Hence, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., Accordingly, this issue answered partly in the affirmative.

9 ISSUE NO.3:
23.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.4,60,500/- (Rupees Four Lakhs sixty thousand five hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of the amount awarded, it is ordered to release the entire compensation amount to the petitioner.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
